item.title: I'm a builder, I can build anything
item.description:
Gordon: I wish people would just tell me exactly what they want and then I would go and build it.
Joe: Like a tailor making a custom suit.
Gordon: Exactly. I can build anything.
Halt and catch fire, s02e04 We truly found ourselves in an unexpected era for software builders. With a snap of a finger and a few prompts “you” can create something. Tokens right now are almost free, major corporations still pumping money into the AI promise, which might, or might not deliver. But damn, the shift. THE SHIFT. As an engineer, I love it and I hate it. There are evenings where I can’t sleep because I think about slopping another project. Another project I would not have had time to even consider. But now? Now the sky is the limit. Um, I mean your 5h window of token usage is the limit. From a personal perspective it can be great - I can resurrect some of my old projects and have fun for a bit, do the maintenance on some of my old libraries with little effort, I can fork stuff and adapt it for my needs so easily it’s laughable. I can build a brand new tool just to solve a single, very particular problem I have been dealing with - and then just forget it ever happened. The flow is gone, but it was replaced by the token nirvana sponsored by codex resets. Is there even a difference, brain?

item.title: Start With One Customer
item.description: If you’ve been into side projects, you’ve probably seen countless times the story of someone building something really big and complex, launching it, and having 0 users. With the AI era we’re living in, this will become even more common since software is cheaper to make. I’ve worked on many side projects over the years, some with big ambitions and some very small, to solve a specific personal challenge. And that’s fine, I love to work on something that allows me to be fully creative without restrictions, but if your goal is to create a business, the starting place needs to be a bit different.
